messages:
Carla: quick sync — proposing we collapse our public status lexicon to three client-facing buckets: OK, Degraded, Unavailable. Keep internal granularity for routing/telemetry but surface only these to customers. thoughts?
Matt: +1 on simplicity for customers. how do you map transient routing falls (e.g., model fallback) vs real quota rejections? they feel different to apps.
Carla: internal plan is: routing fallback -> Degraded, soft quota/slow-down -> Degraded with hint, hard quota/deny -> Unavailable (429 subtype).
Sara: can we add a small machine-readable hint header so SDKs can behave smartly? e.g. `X-RW-Status: degraded;hint=cacheable` or `X-RW-Action: retry-after=5`
Matt: yes please. SDK teams need an unambiguous enum to drive backoff. prefer a single header with structured but short values.
Leo: telemetry/alerting note — please include an immutable token `status_variant` in the payload so ops can distinguish: fallback, quantized, out_of_capacity, quota_hard, quota_soft. We should avoid exposing that in the console copy though.
Carla: agree — console copy stays high-level. ops/telemetry gets `status_variant` via event pipeline. UI uses `Degraded`/`Unavailable` strings only.
Matt: UX question: when do we show the banner versus inline error? if many requests degrade we want an org-level banner; single-route degrade -> inline. Need a small threshold spec.
Sara: threshold idea: >5% error rate for 2m across any route => org banner. otherwise per-route badge. happy to sketch visuals. :paintbrush:
Leo: routing policy implication — fallback paths should set `X-RW-Status-Source: fallback` so we can compute P50 latency of degraded vs normal. Also record `fallback_model` when relevant.
Carla: good call. Also proposal: in console rollout UI, surface a toggle `show_internal_variants` (off by default) for debugging. That way support can flip it without changing API.
Matt: can we standardize numeric codes too? like a 3-digit code space: 1xx internal ok, 2xx client visible ok, 4xx client visible errors, but we only expose the human text. SDKs get the number for programmatic paths.
Sara: I'd rather avoid re-inventing HTTP semantics. Maybe stick with HTTP status + `X-RW-Code` where `X-RW-Code` is a short token (e.g., `Q_HARD`, `ROUT_FALLBACK`).
Carla: agreed — keep HTTP semantics but add `X-RW-Code` tokens. Ops uses tokens, console shows high-level message tied to token mapping.
Matt: small format suggestion for header: `X-RW-Code: Q_HARD;variant=tenant_quota` — semicolon-delimited pairs. easy parse in languages and human readable.
Leo: when recording telemetry events, include `status_text` (public), `rw_code` (token), `variant`, `route`, `model_family`. That gives enough signal to drive alerts and cost dashboards.
Sara: runbook tie-in: each `rw_code` should map to a runbook id. ops-bot can post runbook link when `rw_code` seen in prod. ops-bot: monitoring rule created: when `rw_code: Q_HARD` > 0.1% for 5m => post runbook link to #incidents.
Carla: next steps: I'll draft RFC with examples (response headers, SDK pseudo-code, console toggle UX). tagging @Matt @Sara @Leo for review by EOD tomorrow.
Matt: will review. quick comment: ensure 429 still passes `Retry-After` when relevant.
Sara: and ensure rate-limited responses include `quota_window` so SDKs can show a progress UI.
Leo: add a test plan for telemetry (synthetic that triggers each variant). we can run on staging before rollout.
Carla: thanks all. short followup: should we rename `Degraded` to `Reduced`? feels more actionable to customers.
Matt: prefer `Degraded` — it's common. but not a hill.
Sara: `Reduced` might confuse. +1 for `Degraded`.
Carla: ok `Degraded` it is. I'll drop the RFC into #eng-docs and link here. :sparkles:
